```{python}
#| include: false

def embed_example(q: "Quiz", title: str | None = None, height_offset: int = 50) -> None:
    html = q.to_html(title=title).replace('"', '&quot;')
    print(f"""<iframe srcdoc="{html}" onload='javascript:(function(o){{var _height=o.contentWindow.document.body.scrollHeight+{height_offset};o.style.height=_height+"px";}}(this));' style='overflow: hidden;'></iframe>""")
```

This guide builds questions in Python, collects them in a `Quiz`, and exports Moodle XML.
To write questions as Markdown files instead, see the [Markdown Schema](markdown.qmd); a
Markdown file becomes a question object with `Reader("question.md").read()`.

## Basics

```{python}
from questionsafe import Q, Quiz
```

- `Q` holds the question classes: `Q.SingleChoice`, `Q.MultiChoice`, `Q.TrueFalse`,
  `Q.ShortAnswer`, `Q.Numerical`, `Q.Cloze`, `Q.Essay`, `Q.Description`, `Q.Category`.
- Setters return the question, so calls chain. `set_*` methods replace a value;
  `add_*` methods append one item to a list.
- `questiontext` can be passed to the constructor or set later with `ask()` (an alias of
  `set_questiontext()`).

The previews below are the HTML from `Quiz.to_html()`.

## Question types

### TrueFalse

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
tfq = (
    Q.TrueFalse(
        name="Logic/DeMorgan",
        questiontext="True or False: Not(A and B) == (Not A) or (Not B)"
    )
    .set_correct_if_true()
)
quiz = Quiz([tfq])  # pass a list of questions to the Quiz constructor
quiz.to_html()      # or quiz.to_xml()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(quiz)
```

### SingleChoice

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.SingleChoice("SC")
     .ask("Pick one")
     .set_choice_correct("A")      # one correct choice
     .set_choices_wrong("B", "C")  # several wrong choices
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

- Choice texts may be `Text` values to set their format, e.g.
  `set_choice_correct(Text("**A**", format="markdown"))`; plain strings are HTML.
- `SingleChoice` has exactly one correct choice, at 100%. `add_choice_correct` raises if
  one already exists.

### MultiChoice

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.MultiChoice(name="MC")
     .ask("Pick all that apply")
     .set_choices_correct("A", "B")  # 100% split evenly: 50 each
     .set_choices_wrong("C", "D")
     .set_numbering("123")           # abc (default), ABCD, 123, iii, III or none
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

- `set_choices_correct` splits 100% evenly and snaps to a fraction Moodle allows
  (e.g., 33.33333 for three). `add_choice_correct` re-splits the existing correct choices
  the same way; it raises when they are not even or 100% cannot be split (e.g., 11 ways).
- For uneven fractions, give the answers yourself:

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Answer
mc3 = Q.MultiChoice(name="Math/Primes", questiontext="Pick primes")
mc3.set_answers(
    Answer.from_text("2", fraction=60),
    Answer.from_text("3", fraction=40),
    Answer.from_text("4", fraction=0),
)
mc3.validate()
```

- `set_scoring(rule)` sets every wrong choice by a named rule after R/exams (`false2`,
  `false`, `true`, `all`, `none`).
- `set_single_choice()` shows radio buttons. One choice must be 100%; others may carry
  partial credit, e.g. 100/50/0.
- Choice layout: `set_numbering`, `set_shuffle`, `set_single_choice`, or
  `set_choice_layout(numbering=..., shuffle=..., single_choice=...)`. The defaults are
  Moodle's: numbering `abc`, shuffle on. See the
  [name table](markdown.qmd#choice-layout) for the matching Moodle names.

### ShortAnswer

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.ShortAnswer("SA")
     .ask("Spell 'colour'")
     .add_answer("colour")  # fraction defaults to 100
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

One answer must be worth 100% (for Numerical too), as Moodle's edit form requires. Moodle
grades a response by the first matching answer, so add specific answers before wildcards
such as `*`. `set_usecase(True)` makes matching case-sensitive.

### Numerical

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Numerical("NU")
     .ask("2+2?")
     .add_answer(4)
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

`add_answer(value, tolerance=..., fraction=..., feedback=...)` adds one accepted value;
Moodle grades by the first matching answer.

Answers with units: `add_answer_unit` adds a value in a unit and infers the multiplier.
Unit options are set once per question; the defaults are Moodle's, and the
[Units table](markdown.qmd#units) lists what they mean.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Numerical("Weight")
     .ask("100g + 1kg = ?")
     .add_answer_unit(1100, "g")   # base unit and base answer
     .add_answer_unit(1.1, "kg")   # infers the kg multiplier, 0.001
     # .set_unit_options(handling="optional", penalty=0.1, penalty_of="response",
     #                   input="text", left=False)  # the defaults
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

To list units explicitly, use `add_units()` or `set_units()`:

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
from questionsafe import Unit
(
    Q.Numerical("Speed")
     .ask("Give speed in m/s; km/h allowed")
     .add_answer(3.14)
     .add_units(
         Unit("m/s"),           # base unit
         Unit("km/h", 3.6),     # 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h
         handling="graded", input="select",
     )
)
```

### Cloze

A cloze question embeds other questions (SingleChoice, MultiChoice, ShortAnswer,
Numerical) as gaps. `{{name}}` in the text marks where the question named `name` goes.

```{python}
#| echo: true
gap1 = Q.SingleChoice("gap1").set_choice_correct("Tokyo").set_choices_wrong("Osaka", "Kyoto")
gap2 = Q.MultiChoice("gap2").set_choices_correct("Shinagawa", "Shinjuku").set_choices_wrong("Yokohama")
clz = (
    Q.Cloze("Japan/Cities")
    .ask("The capital of Japan is {{gap1}}. Choose stations in Tokyo: {{gap2}}")
    .embed_question(gap1)
    .embed_question(gap2, orientation="h", weight=2)
)
clz.compile_text()
```

`orientation` picks the widget: for SingleChoice, `None` = dropdown, `"v"`/`"h"` = vertical
or horizontal radio buttons; for MultiChoice, `None`/`"v"` = vertical checkboxes, `"h"` =
horizontal. `weight` is the gap's share of the grade. `set_scoring(rule)` applies a scoring
rule to every embedded choice gap.

### Essay

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Essay("E")
     .ask("<p>Introduce yourself.</p>")
)
```

Essay has setters for the response box (`set_response_format`, `set_input_lines`,
`set_response_template`, ...), attachments (`set_attachments_count`, ...), and grader
information (`set_graderinfo`).

### Description

A description shows information and has no answers.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Description("Desc/Week1")
     .set_questiontext("<p>This section covers basic topics.</p>")
)
```

### Category

A category is not a question: it tells Moodle which question bank category the questions
after it go into.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
Q.Category("$course$/Exam/Final")
```

## Question text formats

Strings are HTML. Use `Text(..., format=...)` for another format.

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Text
Q.SingleChoice(name="SC", questiontext="What is the capital of Thailand?")  # html
Q.MultiChoice(
    name="MC-md",
    questiontext=Text("Pick EU capitals:\n\n- Paris\n- Berlin\n- Madrid", format="markdown"),
)
```

Moodle wraps plain sentences in paragraphs, so `<p>…</p>` can be omitted.

## Answers

`add_answer` takes a string (or a number for Numerical) and keyword options:

```{python}
#| echo: true
mc = (
    Q.MultiChoice(name="Capitals", questiontext="Pick one")
    .add_answer("Tokyo", fraction=100)
    .add_answer("Osaka", fraction=0)
)
nu = Q.Numerical(name="Pi", questiontext="π (two decimals)?").add_answer(3.14, tolerance=0.005)
```

`set_answers` replaces the whole list; build the answers with `Answer.from_text` or
`Answer.from_num`.

## Quizzes

`Quiz` collects questions and categories and exports them.

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Hint
quiz = Quiz(category="Exam/Week1")
quiz.add(
    Q.MultiChoice(name="Capital/Thailand", questiontext="What is the capital of Thailand?")
    .set_choices_correct("Bangkok", feedback="Right!")
    .set_choices_wrong("Chiang Mai", "Phuket", "Pattaya")
    .set_hints(
        Hint("Consider the most populous city.", shownumcorrect=True),
        Hint("Eliminate coastal resort options.", clearwrong=True),
        penalty=0.25,
    )
)
quiz.title = "Combined Preview"
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(quiz)
```

- Export with `quiz.to_xml("out.xml")` and preview with `quiz.to_html("out.html")`.
  `render_xml`/`write_xml` (and the HTML pair) take a plain list of questions instead.
- To override the XML or HTML templates, pass `templates_dir` to the render functions.

### Categories

```{python}
#| echo: true
quiz = Quiz(category="Course/Week1")
quiz.add_category("Intro")                         # $course$/Course/Week1/Intro
quiz.add_category("Intro-Absolute", inherit=False)  # $course$/Intro-Absolute
```

A category path gets `$course$/` in front unless its first segment is already a
`$...$` token.

### Groups of variants

`QuestionGroup` bundles variants of one question; `add_group` puts them in their own
subcategory and assigns idnumbers. `MetaChoice` generates such groups (see
[MetaChoice](metachoice.qmd)).

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe.base import QuestionGroup
v1 = Q.TrueFalse(name="Logic/DM/1", questiontext="...").set_correct_if_true()
v2 = Q.TrueFalse(name="Logic/DM/2", questiontext="...").set_correct_if_true()
quiz = Quiz(category="Course/Week1")
quiz.add_group(QuestionGroup([v1, v2]), idnumber_prefix="dm-", idnumber_offset=0)
```

## Question equality

`q1 == q2` compares every field of two questions of the same class. For choice questions
(MultiChoice, SingleChoice, TrueFalse) the order of the choices is ignored: it is presentation,
not content. For ShortAnswer and Numerical the order counts, because Moodle grades them by
the first matching answer. To compare choice order as well, use `q1.answers == q2.answers`.

Numerical values compare after rounding to 15 decimal places, so `0.3 + 0.3 + 0.3` equals
`0.9`. In the cloze text, values and tolerances are written with 15 significant digits.
To accept nearby values, give an explicit tolerance rather than relying on Moodle's implicit
epsilon for `tolerance=0`.

## Safe API

"Safe" methods keep a question valid: after any chain of them, `validate()` passes. List
them with `list_safe_apis`:

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import list_safe_apis
list_safe_apis(Q.MultiChoice)
```

In many IDEs their tooltips start with "[SAFE]".

## API summary (selected)

- All questions: `set_name`, `set_questiontext`/`ask`, `set_feedback_general`,
  `set_defaultgrade`, `set_tags`/`add_tag`, `set_idnumber`
- Hints and penalties: `add_hint`, `set_hints` (penalty can be `"auto"`), `set_penalty`
- Combined feedback: `set_feedback_combined`, `set_feedback_correct/partiallycorrect/incorrect`
- MultiChoice: `set_choices_correct/wrong`, `add_choice_correct/wrong`, `set_scoring`,
  `set_numbering`, `set_shuffle`, `set_single_choice`, `set_choice_layout`, `set_answers`
- SingleChoice: `set_choice_correct`
- TrueFalse: `set_correct_if_true`, `set_correct_if_false`
- ShortAnswer: `add_answer`, `set_answers`, `set_usecase`
- Numerical: `add_answer`, `add_answer_unit`, `set_units`/`add_units`, `set_unit_options`
- Cloze: `embed_question`, `set_scoring`, `compile_text`

Every class and method is in the [API Reference](api/index.qmd).
